preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= n and int(line.split()[0]) != int(line.split()[1]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct intersections within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == m + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly m + 1 lines: the first line contains n and m, and the next m lines each contain exactly two integers representing a road.
The first line of input contains integers n (number of intersections) and m (number of roads) as specified.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the number of 'damn rhombi' in the graph, where each rhombus is counted exactly once regardless of the order of b and d.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a < c <= n and 1 <= b < n and 1 <= d < n and a != b != c != d != a and b != d and (a, b) in roads and (b, c) in roads and (a, d) in roads and (d, c) in roads and (b, d) not in roads and (d, b) not in roads for a, b, c, d in rhombi)
postconditions.description: For every 'damn rhombus' (a, b, c, d) counted in the output, the intersections a, b, c, d are distinct, and there exist exactly two distinct paths from a to c: one via b and the other via d, with no direct road between b and d.

postconditions.expression: len(rhombi) == int(stdout) and all(a < c for a, b, c, d in rhombi) and all(b < d for a, b, c, d in rhombi)
postconditions.description: The output integer equals the number of unique 'damn rhombi' (a, b, c, d) where a < c and b < d to avoid duplicate counting due to ordering.
